thread:
maria: Heads-up — ironwood13b (int4) canary is spiking OOMs on requests with long prefixes (>1024). Started at 10% canary, now ~12% error rate on canary pods. Logs show memfrag + allocation failures. Repro snippet below.

kevin: Ugh. Is this new quant build or the usual prefetch behavior?

maria: new int4 quant + active prefix prefetch. We pushed the aggressive prefetch heuristic last week (prefetch_window=1.2x). Sample log: 

```
# /var/log/inference/ironwood-canary.log
[2025-04-05T18:12:03Z] ERROR oom: failed alloc 104857600 bytes at gpu_alloc.cc:123
[2025-04-05T18:12:03Z] INFO seq_len=1400 prefetch_slots=32 kv_cache=1.0GB post_frag=0.72
[2025-04-05T18:12:03Z] INFO serving-config: max_new_tokens=512 batch_size=8 prefetch=aggressive
```

sam: Quick experiment results from a local stress run:
- baseline (canary config): OOMs 15% when seq>1200, tail latency p95 420ms
- change: max_new_tokens -> 128, batch_size -> 4, prefetch -> moderate => OOMs 1.2%, p95 455ms
Tradeoff: slight latency regression but much fewer OOMs.

kevin: That suggests we should change per-model defaults rather than revert prefetch globally. Can we set an ironwood profile with conservative defaults?

ciara: Agreed. Proposal:
- model.profile.max_new_tokens = "128"
- model.profile.max_batch_size = "4"
- model.profile.prefetch = "moderate"
- runtime.kv_trim_threshold = "0.6"  # trim earlier
- compactor.interval = "2m"  # more aggressive slot compaction
- fallback.model_variant = "int8" for sessions longer than 800 tokens

maria: Looks good. Also add a soft-evict policy: evict oldest KV segments when free_mem < 1.0GB. That reduced memfrag in my repro.

kevin: Can we add an automated eval in Redwood Optimize that runs the standard convo bench (mix of short+long prompts) against int4 and int8, and records OOM rate + quality diff? Want to detect regressions before canary.

sam: I'll wire up a quick eval. Expect ~2h to produce clean numbers. Will include deterministic seeds and a 50/50 short/long prompt mix.

ops-bot: @maria config-change "ironwood13b: temp-profile" applied to canary pool (10% -> 10%) by ops-bot at 1827654360 :hammer_and_wrench: 

deploy-bot: Rolling canary config update: ironwood13b profile patch -> v1.3-temp (10% traffic) — monitor window 15m.

ciara: We'll also add a metric alert: canary oom_rate > 3% over 10m => auto-rollback. And an anomaly alert on memfrag > 0.65 for >5m.

maria: Plan: merge per-model profile PR (will include the compactor + kv_trim defaults), run Optimize eval, and if eval OOM_rate < 0.5% and quality delta < 0.5% -> promote to 50% canary then full rollout. If OOM_rate spikes we fallback to int8 variant automatically. I'll open PR now and tag @kevin @ciara for review. :thumbsup:

kevin: Thanks — prefer conservative defaults for now. Add a short runbook section describing how to revert to int8 fallback and how to read the memfrag dashboard.

sam: Eval job queued. Posting results in this thread when done.

maria: thanks all — updating the onboarding doc and the release notes. Will follow up with the PR link.

sam: (later) Eval summary: int4 w/ new profile: OOM_rate 0.9% (down from 12%), quality delta vs fp16 = +0.1% BLEU on our conv benchmark, avg latency +6%. int8 fallback shows 0 OOMs but +1.2% quality drop. Recommendation: keep int4 w/ conservative profile and auto-fallback to int8 when session_len>800 or oom_rate alert triggers.

ciara: Good data. I'll add the canary alerts and the compactor tweak to the ops runbook.

maria: PR: https://git.redwood/inference/infra/patches/1234 — contains profile + runbook. Merging after 1h if no objections.

kevin: No objections. Merge on green. :rocket:
